- If sentiment is bullish (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; cap forecast at +10% above peak or adjust downward by 2–3 points.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices when sentiment is bullish; add 1–2% buffer to end of forecast horizon.
- If sentiment alternates sharply (e.g., 1.0 → 0.0 → 1.0), model exhibits lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for bullish sentiment transitions.
- Model overreacts to early sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns bullish after 3–5 days, delay forecast adjustment until 5–7 days later.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5), model often drifts toward mean; apply mean reversion by adjusting forecast toward 30-day average if deviation > 2%.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days: model tends to overestimate; apply 1–2% downward correction for long-term forecasts.
